findings.text: non-blocking: _restore_refused_launch_to_queue re-implements the request write-back that _restore_queued (line 1683) owns — the seven-key pop list, the discard check and the locked _require_live_writeback/_retain_launched_record/_write_pointer sequence — so the two restore paths can drift; _restore_queued should take the hold and skip _stamp_failure rather than be copied.

non-blocking: a ScopeConflict raised by the local-fallback relaunch inside the `except BudgetHold` branch is caught by the generic `except Exception as fallback_error`, leaving hold_only False so _record_queued_failure stamps the failure onto the pointer while it is still in phase starting — the shape this node repairs — whenever a metered hold and a claim taken in the rebind window coincide.
